record.body: On warm wet nights, male frogs gather at ponds and call in chorus, each species with its own call pattern of pulse rate, pitch, and timing, so that females can find males of their own species in a mixed chorus. Chorusing is energetically expensive and attracts predators as well as mates, which is why males often time their calls to avoid overlapping a neighbour's call or, in some species, deliberately overlap to compete. Temperature matters: in many frogs the pulse rate of the call rises as body temperature rises, so a recording of call rate can carry information about conditions as well as identity. This record covers biophony, the frogs' own chorus, distinct from the geophony of rain and running water at the same pond and from anthrophony such as nearby road noise, which can mask frog calls.

demo.code:
TITLE = 'Frog Choruses: Many Voices, One Night'
N = 30
SEC = 1
DUR = 2.0
per_sec = N / SEC
per_min = per_sec * 60.0
duty = N * DUR / SEC
total = per_sec * DUR
print('Record: ' + TITLE)
print('Count: %d in %d seconds' % (N, SEC))
print('Rate: %.2f per second, %.2f per minute' % (per_sec, per_min))
print('Duty cycle: %.3f' % duty)
print('Total in one call of %.1f seconds: %.1f' % (DUR, total))
